newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude looks bearish in medium-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude looks bearish in medium-term.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - JUNE 25 --------
+ Crude was expected to oscillate around the $19 level on Wednesday but chartists said the medium-term trend was down.
+ Gasoline was expected to range trade with support at 55.40 cents and resistance at 56.20 cents.
+ Heat support seen at 51.50 cents resistance at 56.20 cents.
NYMEX crude futures were expected to consolidate on Wednesday after minor losses on Tuesday but many chartist thought the direction in the medium-term was down.
August NYMEX crude closed nine cents lower at $19.03 a barrel, July gasoline heating oil ended a 0.35 cent off at 51.57 cents a gallon and July gasoline a 0.03 cent off at 55.68 cents a gallon.

"We might see it heading up to the $19.30 area as the market relieves some of its oversold positions but ultimately I think the trend is down with a target in the $18 range," said a Washington-based chartist.
Other chartists were equally bearish in their assessments.

"Preparation is still negative so we continue to sell rallies up to $19.16 waiting for a buying extreme to prompt us to cover or a break back above $19.16 forces us to cut," analysts at MeesPierson in London said in their daily report.
They pegged resistance at $19.16, $19.40 and $19.52 and support at $18.96, $18.84 and $18.64.
Gasoline was seen stuck in range.
"In essence, choppy range-trading continues with an upward bias for the next leg," said Al Graham at Elliott Wave International in Gainesville, Georgia in his daily report.
He pegged support at 55.10, 54.84/80 and 54.05 cents while resistance was seen around 56.20/30/40, 57.15/51 and 59.15 cents.
Analysts at Mees Pierson pegged support for July gasoline at 55.40, 54.90 and 51.00 cents and resistance around 56.20, 56.50 and 57.10 cents.
Heating oil was also expected to head sideways to lower in the next few days, but most saw the market at the beck and call of gasoline and crude.

"We would therefore only buy if gasoline and WTI managed to improve inwhich case we look to buy on dips to 51.30 cents waiting to take profits and go short at 52.30 cents. If the other markets remain weak we simply trade the other way shorting the market at 52.30 cents first," said analysts at MeesPierson. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
